ਮੇਰਾ ਗੁਰੁ ਪਰਮੇਸਰੁ ਸੁਖਦਾਈ ॥:
Declaring the identity of the spiritual guide with the Supreme Transcendent Lord, praising the Guru as the absolute embodiment of the Divine. Proclaiming the spiritual master to be the ultimate dispenser of peace, bliss, and supreme comfort. The stance is one of reverent affirmation, recognizing God made accessible through the Guru who resolves all affliction and bestows complete contentment upon the devotee.

Themes: guru parameshar, divine oneness, spiritual guide, giver of peace, supreme bliss, contentment, devotional praise
ਤੁਮ ਦਾਤੇ ਤੁਮ ਪੁਰਖ ਬਿਧਾਤੇ ॥:
Praising and addressing the Divine directly as the supreme provider, the all-pervading primal being, and the creator who ordains the destiny of all creation. It acknowledges complete dependence on God as the generous source of all gifts, the omnipresent reality permeating all living beings, and the sovereign architect governing fate, life, and existence.

Themes: divine benevolence, supreme creator, architect of destiny, all-pervading Lord, total dependence, praise of God, universal provider
ਕਰੁਣਾ ਮੈ ਕਿਰਪਾਲ ਕ੍ਰਿਪਾ ਨਿਧਿ ਜੀਵਨ ਪਦ ਨਾਨਕ:
Praises the Divine as the embodiment of compassion, merciful Lord, and boundless ocean of grace, while yearning for the blessed vision (darshan). Beholding the Divine Presence bestows spiritual revitalization, liberation in life (jeevan pad), and the highest state of spiritual consciousness. Contemplation and divine sight grant true life, fulfilling the devotee through boundless divine mercy.

Themes: darshan (divine vision), divine grace, compassion, spiritual liberation, jeevan pad (supreme spiritual state), yearning for God
ਤੂੰ ਭਾਰੋ ਠਾਕੁਰੁ ਗੁਣੀ ਗਹੇਰਾ ॥੨॥:
Directly addressing and glorifying God as the supreme Master who is immensely great, weighty, and an unfathomable ocean of virtues. Praising the Divine for boundless majesty, profound depth of character, and limitless moral and spiritual excellence. Acknowledging the absolute grandeur and profound nature of the Creator in humble adoration and reverent awe.

Themes: divine virtues, greatness of God, praise and adoration, sovereignty of the Master, unfathomable depth, humility, reverence
ਦੇਵਣਹਾਰੁ ਦਾਤਾਰੁ ਕਿਤੁ ਮੁਖਿ ਸਾਲਾਹੀਐ ॥:
Declaring the sheer impossibility of adequately praising the supreme Benefactor who provides sustenance to all living beings. The seeker asks in awe and humble inadequacy with what mouth or tongue one could ever fully celebrate and extol such an infinitely generous Provider. It emphasizes the ineffability of the Divine's boundless giving and the profound limitation of human speech to honor true divine benevolence.

Themes: supreme provider, ineffability, praising the divine, infinite generosity, humility, adoration, universal sustainer
ਤੇਰੇ ਕਵਨ ਕਵਨ ਗੁਣ ਕਹਿ ਕਹਿ ਗਾਵਾ ਤੂ ਸਾਹਿਬ ਗ:
Adoring and singing praise of the Divine while marveling at God's limitless attributes. Acknowledges the Lord and Master as the infinite treasure of all virtues and excellence, wondering rhetorically which glories can possibly be recounted when they are boundless. Expresses humble awe before the sovereign Creator who embodies all perfection and sustains everything.

Themes: praising divine virtues, infinite qualities of God, treasure of excellence, wonder and awe, boundless glory, devotion, sovereign Lord
ਰੇ ਬਉਰੇ ਤੁਹਿ ਘਰੀ ਨ ਰਾਖੈ ਕੋਈ ॥:
Admonishing and warning the deluded mortal mind about the harsh reality of death and bodily impermanence. Once life departs, not a single relative or companion will permit the dead body to remain inside the house even for a brief moment or single instant. It urges waking from the madness of worldly delusion, emphasizing the fleeting nature of physical existence and the immediate rejection and disposal of the corpse by earthly relations.

Themes: death and mortality, impermanence of the body, illusion of worldly relations, admonishing the mind, transient physical existence, corpse disposal, detachment from maya
ਕਾਹੇ ਮਨ ਤੂ ਡੋਲਤਾ ਹਰਿ ਮਨਸਾ ਪੂਰਣਹਾਰੁ ॥:
Admonishes one's own mind to abandon anxiety, doubt, and wavering faith. Reassures the restless consciousness that the Divine satisfies all longings, sustains creation, and fulfills every inner desire. Urges steadfast trust and spiritual stability in divine providence instead of succumbing to worry, fear, and mental instability.

Themes: mental stability, overcoming anxiety, faith in providence, fulfiller of desires, counseling the mind, divine reassurance, trust in God
ਰੇ ਮਨ ਤੂ ਭੀ ਭਜੁ ਗੋਬਿੰਦ ॥੨॥:
Admonishes and instructs one's own mind to engage in constant simran (loving remembrance) and devotion toward Gobind, the Lord of the universe. Exhorts the inner consciousness to turn away from distraction, participate in continuous meditation, and worship the Divine Sovereign. Urges the self to contemplate God with heartfelt dedication, seeking spiritual focus through vibrating upon the sacred presence of the Creator.

Themes: mind control, self-admonition, simran, divine remembrance, devotion, Gobind, meditation, inner awakening
ਮਨ ਮੇਰਿਆ ਅੰਤਰਿ ਤੇਰੈ ਨਿਧਾਨੁ ਹੈ ਬਾਹਰਿ ਵਸਤੁ:
Admonishing one's own mind to cease seeking fulfillment externally, urging an inward turn toward spiritual truth. The supreme treasure of the Divine, the source of all peace and spiritual wealth, dwells inside the self rather than in the outside world, physical wandering, or worldly pursuits. True realization requires looking deep within one's own heart and consciousness rather than searching outward.

Themes: inner treasure, divine presence within, inward search, mind admonition, seeking God inside, rejecting external wandering, spiritual wealth
ਸੁਣਿ ਬਾਵਰੇ ਤੂ ਕਾਏ ਦੇਖਿ ਭੁਲਾਨਾ ॥:
Directly admonishing the spiritually deluded, insane human mind to wake up and listen. The seeker is warned against losing their way and wandering off the righteous spiritual path by gazing upon the fleeting allure of maya (worldly illusion and material attachment). It confronts mortal foolishness, challenging why one becomes intoxicated, mad, and blinded by transient worldly sights.

Themes: spiritual delusion, admonishing the mind, maya, worldly illusion, waking up, spiritual wandering, ignorance
ਸੁਣਿ ਬਾਵਰੇ ਥੀਉ ਰੇਣੁ ਜਿਨੀ ਪ੍ਰਭੁ ਧਿਆਇਆ ॥:
Admonishing the deluded, foolish mind to listen and abandon ego through utter humility. Directs the mortal to become the dust of the feet of devout worshippers who meditate upon the Divine. Urges absolute self-effacement, deep veneration of God-conscious saints, and seeking refuge in holy congregation (sangat) to attain spiritual union and cure spiritual madness.

Themes: humility, dust of the feet, meditation, holy congregation, eliminating ego, self-effacement, spiritual awakening
ਲਖ ਖੁਸੀਆ ਪਾਤਿਸਾਹੀਆ ਜੇ ਸਤਿਗੁਰੁ ਨਦਰਿ ਕਰੇਇ:
Receiving a single glance of grace (nadar) from the True Guru yields supreme joy and bliss equivalent to ruling hundreds of thousands of royal kingdoms. Declares that divine favor and spiritual benevolence completely surpass all earthly pleasures, sovereign empires, and worldly wealth. Finding spiritual acceptance through the Guru's compassionate sight bestows ultimate fulfillment, rendering material sovereignty and regal enjoyments insignificant by comparison.

Themes: glance of grace, True Guru, nadar, royal sovereignty, supreme bliss, spiritual fulfillment, divine favor
ਸਤਿਗੁਰੁ ਹੋਇ ਦਇਆਲੁ ਤਾ ਦੁਖੁ ਨ ਜਾਣੀਐ ॥:
Declaring the transformative effect of the Satguru's (true spiritual guide's) grace and compassion. When the Guru becomes merciful and showers divine favor, suffering ceases to be felt, and pain is no longer recognized or experienced as affliction. Spiritual benevolence eradicates all agony and mental distress, granting immunity from worldly grief and sorrow.

Themes: guru's grace, mercy and compassion, eradication of suffering, freedom from pain, spiritual tranquility, satguru, transcendence of sorrow
ਹਰਿ ਚਉਥੜੀ ਲਾਵ ਮਨਿ ਸਹਜੁ ਭਇਆ ਹਰਿ ਪਾਇਆ ਬਲਿ:
Announces the final stage of spiritual union through the metaphor of the fourth marriage round, where the mind achieves sahaj (intuitive spiritual poise and tranquil equilibrium). Declares the complete realization and attainment of the Divine, expressing ecstatic surrender and devotion unto the Lord. The soul-bride reaches supreme fulfillment, inner stillness, and permanent oneness with God.

Themes: fourth laav, spiritual marriage, sahaj, union with God, soul-bride, inner peace, divine realization, devotional surrender
ਸੁਖੁ ਪਾਇਆ ਸਤਿਗੁਰੂ ਮਨਾਇ ॥:
Attaining supreme peace, bliss, and spiritual fulfillment by pleasing the Satguru (the True Guru) and enshrining the Guru within the heart. Declaring that inner tranquility, satisfaction of all desires, and lasting contentment result directly from surrendering to the divine teacher's will and living in loving devotion and alignment with the Guru's guidance.

Themes: Satguru, pleasing the Guru, attaining peace, sukh, devotion, spiritual fulfillment, surrender, inner tranquility
ਸਤਿਗੁਰੁ ਮੇਰਾ ਸਦਾ ਸਹਾਈ ਜਿਨਿ ਦੁਖ ਕਾ ਕਾਟਿਆ:
Declaring absolute reliance on and gratitude toward the Satguru (True Guru) as an eternal protector, ally, and constant helper. The Guru uproots the very source, omen, and banner of suffering, destroying the root of pain and sorrow for anyone seeking spiritual refuge. Through divine sanctuary, distress and misfortune are permanently eliminated.

Themes: Satguru, divine protection, eradicating suffering, refuge in the Guru, eternal helper, liberation from distress
ਗੋਬਿੰਦ ਮਿਲਣ ਕੀ ਇਹ ਤੇਰੀ ਬਰੀਆ ॥:
Urges and admonishes the mortal that the current human existence is the supreme turn and singular opportunity to meet God. It declares the ultimate purpose of human incarnation: achieving divine union with the Creator before time runs out. The soul is directly reminded to seize this rare window of life for spiritual realization rather than wasting it in worldly delusion.

Themes: human birth purpose, divine union, opportunity for realization, urgency of spiritual practice, meeting God, impermanence of life
ਪ੍ਰਾਣੀ ਤੂੰ ਆਇਆ ਲਾਹਾ ਲੈਣਿ ॥:
Admonishing the mortal being by reminding them of the true objective of human birth. Earthly incarnation is framed as a commercial endeavor where the soul is sent to earn the spiritual wealth and profit of naam (the divine Name). It directly addresses the individual to awaken them to life's ultimate spiritual mission and divine purpose.

Themes: purpose of human life, spiritual profit, divine Name, commercial metaphor, awakening the mortal, remembrance, spiritual earning
ਹਰਿ ਭਗਤਿ ਦ੍ਰਿੜੁ ਮਿਲੁ ਸਾਧ ਨਾਨਕ ਤੇਰੈ ਕਾਮਿ:
Instructing the human soul to join the sadh (holy preceptor or company of the devout) and firmly cultivate devotional worship of Hari (the Lord God) within the heart. It declares that divine devotion is the only pursuit of lasting value that will ultimately assist, serve, and benefit the mortal in the spiritual realm and beyond worldly life.

Themes: devotional worship, holy congregation, Guru, lasting spiritual benefit, bhakti, soul's ultimate purpose, spiritual assistance
ਜੀਵਨਾ ਸਫਲ ਜੀਵਨ ਸੁਨਿ ਹਰਿ ਜਪਿ ਜਪਿ ਸਦ ਜੀਵਨਾ:
Declares human life truly fruitful and fulfilled only through listening to the divine Name and engaging in continuous simran (meditative remembrance) of God. Constant chanting and meditating upon Hari brings eternal spiritual life, making mortal existence purposeful, victorious, and spiritually alive rather than deadened in worldly oblivion. True existence is living in ceaseless devotion.

Themes: purposeful life, fruitful human birth, listening to Naam, continuous remembrance, spiritual immortality, chanting Hari, simran
ਚਰਨ ਕਮਲ ਆਧਾਰੁ ਜਨ ਕਾ ਆਸਰਾ ॥:
Declares that the lotus feet of the Divine—signifying sanctuary, loving surrender, and divine presence—serve as the total foundation, sustenance, and anchor for humble devotees. Affirms absolute dependence upon the Lord, portraying divine presence as the faithful servant's true life support, shelter, and enduring spiritual refuge.

Themes: lotus feet, divine refuge, support of devotees, spiritual sustenance, total surrender, reliance on God
ਚਰਨ ਕਮਲ ਸੇਵੀ ਰਿਦ ਅੰਤਰਿ ਗੁਰ ਪੂਰੇ ਕੈ ਆਧਾਰਿ:
Supplicates for grace to contemplate and cherish the Lord's lotus feet—the sanctuary of divine presence and humble surrender—within the heart. Leaning entirely upon the shelter and support of the perfect spiritual guide, it commits to inner meditation, deep devotion, and continuous loving remembrance. Finding refuge in the Guru enables unceasing enshrinement of the divine Name within one's consciousness.

Themes: lotus feet, Guru's support, heart contemplation, divine sanctuary, devotion, supplication, spiritual shelter
ਚਰਨ ਕਮਲ ਸਿਉ ਪ੍ਰੀਤਿ ਰੀਤਿ ਸੰਤਨ ਮਨਿ ਆਵਏ ਜੀਉ:
Declares the sacred discipline and inner conduct of the saints, whose minds are permanently anchored in loving devotion to the divine lotus feet, the sanctuary of God's presence. Praises the holy beings who cultivate continuous spiritual love, enshrining divine remembrance and humble surrender as their core way of life and mental dwelling.

Themes: lotus feet, divine love, saints, spiritual discipline, surrender, devotion, inner consciousness, holy lifestyle
ਬੋਹਿਥੜਾ ਹਰਿ ਚਰਣ ਮਨ ਚੜਿ ਲੰਘੀਐ ॥:
Admonishing and instructing one's own mind to take refuge in the Divine presence, portrayed as a sturdy boat or ship carrying the soul safely across the turbulent world-ocean of maya (worldly illusion). Surrendering at the Lord's feet provides the vessel of spiritual deliverance, ensuring safe passage across earthly existence and liberation from the cycle of transmigration through complete devotion and sanctuary.

Themes: lotus feet, world ocean, spiritual boat, liberation, taking refuge, instructing the mind, overcoming maya, salvation
ਹਰਿ ਚਰਨ ਕਮਲ ਮਨੁ ਬੇਧਿਆ ਕਿਛੁ ਆਨ ਨ ਮੀਠਾ ਰਾਮ:
Declares total absorption and ecstatic devotion, expressing how the mind is pierced, captivated, and completely enchanted by the divine presence, imaged as lotus feet or sacred sanctuary. Through this deep spiritual surrender, the Sovereign Lord alone tastes sweet and delightful, rendering all other worldly objects, pleasures, and attachments to maya (worldly illusion) tasteless and insignificant in comparison.

Themes: charan kamal (lotus feet), divine sweetness, detachment from maya, spiritual absorption, single-minded devotion, surrender to God, divine sovereignty
ਪੀ ਅੰਮ੍ਰਿਤੁ ਆਘਾਨਿਆ ਗੁਰਿ ਅਮਰੁ ਕਰਾਇਆ ॥੨॥:
Partaking of amrit (the ambrosial nectar of divine virtues), the seeker attains complete spiritual satiety and lasting fulfillment. Through the Guru's guidance and grace, one is rendered immortal, achieving eternal life beyond the cycles of spiritual decay, pain, and death. The mind's thirst is quenched entirely by internalizing the sacred essence.

Themes: amrit nectar, spiritual fulfillment, Guru's grace, immortality, overcoming death, divine contentment, spiritual liberation
ਜਿਨ੍ਹ ਪੀਆ ਸੇ ਮਸਤ ਭਏ ਹੈ ਤੂਟੇ ਬੰਧਨ ਫਾਹੇ ॥:
Drinking the ambrosial nectar of naam (the divine Name) induces spiritual intoxication and supreme bliss. Partaking in this divine essence shatters the shackles of maya (worldly attachment and illusion), snapping all worldly nooses, traps, and entanglements. Declares the liberating outcome of inner immersion in divine consciousness, where spiritual thirst is quenched, mortal bondage is severed, and the soul attains ecstatic freedom.

Themes: naam ras, divine nectar, spiritual intoxication, liberation, breaking worldly bonds, severance of maya, ecstatic freedom
ਹਰਿ ਅੰਮ੍ਰਿਤੁ ਸੋ ਚਖੈ ਮੇਰੇ ਮਨਾ ॥੨॥:
Addressing one's own mind, this declaration identifies the soul who drinks and tastes the immortal nectar of the Divine. Partaking of the life-giving ambrosial water of God brings true spiritual nourishment and vitality, transforming the inner self through direct experiential absorption and consumption of the divine Name (naam).

Themes: amrit (ambrosial nectar), spiritual nourishment, experiencing naam, addressing the mind, divine sweetness, spiritual vitality, tasting the Divine
ਹਰਿ ਰਸੁ ਪੀਵਹੁ ਭਾਈ ॥:
Directly exhorts and instructs spiritual companions and seekers to drink the sublime elixir of the Divine. It urges fellow devotees to imbibe the sweet nectar of naam (the divine Name), seeking refuge in the Guru and continuously tasting the blissful essence of God through meditative remembrance and contemplation.

Themes: drinking divine nectar, har ras, spiritual exhortation, naam simran, divine sweetness, brotherhood of seekers, spiritual instruction
ਗੁਰਿ ਅੰਮ੍ਰਿਤੁ ਹਰਿ ਮੁਖਿ ਚੋਇਆ ਮੇਰੀ ਜਿੰਦੁੜੀ:
Addressing one's own soul to celebrate spiritual rebirth through the Guru's grace. The Guru drops the life-giving amrit (ambrosial nectar of the divine Name) into the seeker's mouth, reviving and reanimating a soul dying of spiritual death into vibrant spiritual life and renewed consciousness. It proclaims the transformative power of divine remembrance in resurrecting fallen, dead minds.

Themes: amrit (ambrosial nectar), spiritual rebirth, guru grace, reviving the dead soul, naam (divine Name), spiritual awakening, transformation
ਅੰਮ੍ਰਿਤੁ ਨਾਮੁ ਨਿਧਾਨੁ ਹੈ ਮਿਲਿ ਪੀਵਹੁ ਭਾਈ ॥:
An earnest exhortation instructing spiritual seekers and companions to gather together in holy congregation (sangat) and collectively partake of the life-giving nectar of naam (the divine Name). It declares the divine Name to be the ultimate inexhaustible treasure and an immortalizing elixir, urging seekers to drink deeply of this spiritual ambrosia through collective meditation and shared devotion.

Themes: amrit (divine nectar), naam (divine Name), spiritual treasure, sangat (holy fellowship), collective devotion, seeking immortality
ਜਨਮ ਮਰਣ ਭਉ ਕਟਿਓਨੁ ਫਿਰਿ ਜੋਨਿ ਨ ਪਾਏ ॥:
Declares the liberating grace of the Divine, who shatters the terrifying dread of birth and death and frees the devotee from entering the cycle of reincarnation again. The soul is redeemed from the repetitive round of transmigration and worldly rebirth, attaining ultimate release and permanent freedom from existential fear and mortality.

Themes: liberation, reincarnation, fear of death, transmigration, ending rebirth, divine grace, mukti, freedom from mortality
ਸਹਜੁ ਭਇਆ ਪ੍ਰਭੁ ਪਾਇਆ ਜਮ ਕਾ ਭਉ ਲਥਾ ॥੨੦॥:
Declaring the spiritual liberation and fruit that arises from attaining sahaj (intuitive poise and inner stillness): realization of the Divine dissolves all terror of death and the Messenger of Death (jam). Attaining God through mental equilibrium and spiritual composure completely eradicates the dread of mortality, judgment, and spiritual death, bringing absolute fearlessness.

Themes: sahaj intuitive poise, attaining God, fear of death, jam messenger of death, fearlessness, spiritual liberation, inner peace
ਜਨਮ ਮਰਣ ਭਉ ਕਟੀਐ ਜਨ ਕਾ ਸਬਦੁ ਜਪਿ ॥:
Reciting and contemplating the sacred Word (shabad) of the Lord's humble servant cuts away the dread of mortality and the agony of the cycle of birth and death. Meditating on divine praise within holy company destroys existential terror, liberating the soul from transmigration and releasing the seeker from the lifelong fear of dying.

Themes: liberation from reincarnation, overcoming fear of death, sacred Word, shabad, divine meditation, humble servant, freedom from transmigration, spiritual remedy
ਨ ਦਨੋਤਿ ਜਸਮਰਣੇਨ ਜਨਮ ਜਰਾਧਿ ਮਰਣ ਭਇਅੰ ॥੧॥ ਰ:
Declaring that simran (loving remembrance) of the Divine destroys all existential suffering and fear. Meditating on the Lord liberates the seeker from the torment of reincarnation (birth and death), the infirmity of old age, mental distress, and the terror of mortality. Contemplative devotion immunizes the mind against dread, anxiety, and worldly affliction, granting absolute spiritual peace and freedom from pain.

Themes: simran, conquering fear of death, cycle of birth and death, overcoming suffering, old age and infirmity, divine remembrance, spiritual liberation
ਜਨਮ ਮਰਣ ਦੁਖੁ ਕਾਟੀਐ ਪਿਆਰੇ ਚੂਕੈ ਜਮ ਕੀ ਕਾਣੇ:
Declaring spiritual liberation from the cycle of birth and death (transmigration) and freedom from the terror and subjugation of the messenger of death (Jamraj). The agony of continuous reincarnation and lifelong suffering is severed, freeing the soul from fear and the oppressive authority of mortality. Addresses the beloved companion with the promise of complete deliverance and ultimate relief from existential dread.

Themes: liberation from reincarnation, messenger of death, transmigration, ending suffering, freedom from fear, spiritual deliverance, mortality
ਜਨਮ ਮਰਣ ਭੈ ਲਾਥੇ ॥੪॥੨॥੫੨॥:
Declaring complete liberation from the cycle of birth and death, announcing that all dread of mortality and transmigration has been permanently removed. It celebrates the attainment of fearlessness and spiritual emancipation where existential terror vanishes, ending the agonizing cycle of continuous dying and reincarnating into the world.

Themes: fear of death, cycle of rebirth, transmigration, spiritual liberation, overcoming fear, fearlessness, release from mortality
ਸਾਧਸੰਗਤਿ ਕੈ ਆਸਰੈ ਪ੍ਰਭ ਸਿਉ ਰੰਗੁ ਲਾਏ ॥:
Declares how taking shelter and refuge in sadhsangat (the company of the devout and holy) enables one to cultivate deep devotion and fall in love with the Divine. Seeking the fellowship of saints nurtures spiritual affection and attachment to God, awakening heartfelt adoration through sacred association and righteous community.

Themes: sadhsangat, divine love, devotion, holy company, spiritual refuge, communion with God, spiritual transformation
ਸਾਧੂ ਸੰਗਿ ਤਰੀਜੈ ਸਾਗਰੁ ਕਟੀਐ ਜਮ ਕੀ ਫਾਸਾ ਜੀ:
Declares that joining the company of the devout (saadh sangat) enables one to cross over the terrifying worldly ocean of illusion and severs the lethal noose of mortality and the messenger of death. Holy association grants liberation from reincarnation and worldly dread, freeing the soul from spiritual bondage and mortal entrapment.

Themes: saadh sangat, holy congregation, crossing the ocean, world ocean, noose of death, liberation, overcoming mortality, spiritual freedom
ਸਾਧਸੰਗਤਿ ਕੀ ਭੀਰ ਜਉ ਪਾਈ ਤਉ ਨਾਨਕ ਹਰਿ ਸੰਗਿ:
Declaring that union with God occurs through joining the fellowship of the holy. Entering the gathering of the devout (saadh sangat) serves as the direct catalyst for meeting, blending, and spiritually merging with the Divine. Testifying to the transformative power of holy company, asserting that spiritual realization and intimate connection with the Lord are attained through association with enlightened beings.

Themes: saadh sangat, company of the holy, union with God, spiritual congregation, merging with the Divine, liberation through saints, divine realization
ਸੰਤਤ ਹੀ ਸਤਸੰਗਤਿ ਸੰਗ ਸੁਰੰਗ ਰਤੇ ਜਸੁ ਗਾਵਤ ਹ:
Portraying the sublime state of holy seekers who remain constantly immersed in satsangat (the company of the devout). Dyed deeply in the vibrant hue of divine love and celestial affection, the saints continuously sing the praises and glories of the Lord. It celebrates spiritual fellowship, devotional singing, sacred musical praise, and unceasing absorption in divine adoration alongside righteous companions.

Themes: satsangat (holy congregation), divine praise, spiritual love, devotional singing, fellowship of saints, constant remembrance, spiritual absorption
ਕਾਢਿ ਲੀਏ ਪ੍ਰਭ ਆਨ ਬਿਖੈ ਤੇ ਸਾਧਸੰਗਿ ਮਨੁ ਲਾਵ:
Praising God's redemptive power while imploring divine rescue from sensory poisons and worldly corruption. The soul is extracted from the toxic mire of vice and sensual desires (bikhai) and anchored in sadhsangat (the company of the holy). It declares that liberation from moral degradation occurs when divine grace redirects the wandering mind away from corrupt distractions into sacred fellowship and spiritual congregation.

Themes: sadhsangat, overcoming vice, divine deliverance, sensory detachment, purifying the mind, company of the holy, grace
ਮਹਿਮਾ ਸਾਧੂ ਸੰਗ ਕੀ ਸੁਨਹੁ ਮੇਰੇ ਮੀਤਾ ॥:
Urges companions and spiritual seekers to attentively hear and absorb the praise, greatness, and transformative glory of the saadh sangat (the company of the holy). It functions as a loving address and call to spiritual awakening, inviting the listener to understand the supreme spiritual value, virtues, and purifying power found within the gathering of the devout.

Themes: saadh sangat (company of the holy), spiritual fellowship, listening to truth, praising the saints, communion, spiritual guidance, divine greatness
ਸੰਤ ਜਨਾ ਕੀ ਰੇਣੁਕਾ ਲੈ ਮਾਥੈ ਲਾਵਉ ॥੧॥ ਰਹਾਉ:
A devotee resolves and yearns to take the dust from the feet of the saints and apply it to their forehead. Expressing supreme humility, reverence, and surrender to the holy, this aspiration seeks sanctification and spiritual purification through the company of the devout (sangat). Venerating the feet of the righteous is embraced as the ultimate blessing, supreme treasure, and refuge for eliminating ego.

Themes: saintly foot dust, charan dhoor, humility, holy company, spiritual purification, surrendering ego, devotion, seeking blessing
ਗੁਰਸਿਖਾਂ ਕੀ ਹਰਿ ਧੂੜਿ ਦੇਹਿ ਹਮ ਪਾਪੀ ਭੀ ਗਤਿ:
Pleading with the Divine for the blessed dust of the feet of the Guru's disciples. The seeker confesses their own sinful, flawed nature and begs for spiritual elevation, redemption, and liberation through association with the holy congregation (sangat). Imploring grace through radical humility and deep reverence for true devotees, this prayer seeks salvation and purification for even the most corrupt souls.

Themes: charan dhoor (dust of feet), humility, prayer for liberation, redemption of sinners, sangat (holy company), divine grace, spiritual elevation
ਕਰਉ ਨਮਸਕਾਰ ਭਗਤ ਜਨ ਧੂਰਿ ਮੁਖਿ ਲਾਵਉ ॥੩॥:
Expressing profound humility and reverence by bowing before the devotees of the Divine and applying the sacred dust of their feet (charan dhoor) to one's face and forehead. Seeking spiritual sanctification, ego dissolution, and self-effacement through venerating the saints and joining the sadhsangat (company of the devout). Actively surrendering personal pride and seeking blessing through the humble servitude of holy beings.

Themes: humility, dust of the saints, sadhsangat, surrender of ego, devotion, reverence for devotees, spiritual purification
ਟਹਲ ਕਰਉ ਤੇਰੇ ਦਾਸ ਕੀ ਪਗ ਝਾਰਉ ਬਾਲ ॥:
Expressing intense longing for humble servitude, the devotee prays to serve the servants of the Divine, wiping the dust from their feet with their own hair. This striking image of self-effacement signifies total surrender, the eradication of ego, and deep reverence for holy devotees. Serving the Lord's servant is embraced as the highest expression of love and spiritual humility.

Themes: seva (selfless service), humility, serving devotees, surrendering ego, sadhsangat (holy congregation), devotion, spiritual submission
ਕਰਿ ਕਿਰਪਾ ਧੂਰਿ ਦੇਹੁ ਸੰਤਨ ਕੀ ਸੁਖੁ ਨਾਨਕੁ ਇ:
Pleading for divine grace and mercy to obtain the dust of the feet of holy saints, longing for the supreme peace and tranquility found in utmost humility and devotion. A prayer yearning for the blessing of serving the devout in the holy company, viewing complete self-effacement before enlightened beings as the ultimate spiritual comfort and true fulfillment.

Themes: longing for humility, dust of the saints' feet, divine grace, plea for peace, service to the holy, surrender, spiritual solace
ਸੰਤਹ ਚਰਣ ਹਮਾਰੋ ਮਾਥਾ ਨੈਨ ਦਰਸੁ ਤਨਿ ਧੂਰਿ ਪਰ:
Pleading for utter humility, total surrender, and devotion in the company of the holy (sangat). The seeker prays that their forehead rests upon the feet of the saints, their eyes constantly behold the blessed vision (darshan) of the devout, and their body is covered with holy foot-dust (charan dhoor). This expresses complete ego elimination, reverent servitude, and physical and spiritual yearning for saintly association.

Themes: humility, charan dhoor (dust of the feet), darshan (sacred vision), sangat (holy congregation), ego surrender, devotion, saints
ਅਤਿ ਸੁੰਦਰ ਮਨਮੋਹਨ ਪਿਆਰੇ ਸਭਹੂ ਮਧਿ ਨਿਰਾਰੇ ॥:
Adoring the Divine through praise of supreme beauty and charming grace, acknowledging the Lord as the beloved fascinator of the mind who is simultaneously immanent and transcendent. Celebrates the paradox of the Creator dwelling intimately within all beings and creation while remaining entirely detached, untainted, and distinct from all worldly existence.

Themes: divine beauty, immanence and transcendence, mind-captivating beloved, omnipresence, detachment, praise and adoration
ਤੇਰਾ ਨਾਮੁ ਰੂੜੋ ਰੂਪੁ ਰੂੜੋ ਅਤਿ ਰੰਗ ਰੂੜੋ ਮੇ:
Directly praising and adoring the Divine in aesthetic wonder and devotion. The Lord’s naam (divine Name) is exalted as supremely beautiful, His manifest form and presence are radiantly lovely, and His love and spiritual color are deeply enchanting. Celebrates the sheer attractiveness, sweetness, and intoxicating delight of God's being, expressing total fascination with the Beloved.

Themes: divine beauty, praise and adoration, naam, divine love, spiritual ecstasy, aesthetic wonder, loving devotion
ਸੁੰਦਰ ਰਸਾਲ ਤੂ ॥੧॥:
Directly praising and adoring the Divine as supremely beautiful, captivating, and the ultimate fountainhead of all spiritual sweetness and delight. The speaker addresses God in reverent awe, identifying the Creator as the boundless source of ambrosial nectar (amrit) and sublime bliss, unmatched in grace, magnificence, and heavenly joy.

Themes: divine beauty, divine adoration, source of nectar, spiritual sweetness, supreme bliss, devotion, praise of God
ਨੈਣ ਪਸੰਦੋ ਸੋਇ ਪੇਖਿ ਮੁਸਤਾਕ ਭਈ ॥:
Expresses the soul-bride's rapturous adoration and spiritual intoxication upon beholding the Divine Beloved. Gazing upon the Creator brings supreme delight to the eyes, captivating the heart and filling the inner self with ecstatic longing and enchanting love. Visual contemplation of divine presence becomes a direct experience of mystical bliss, captivation, and deep devotional attachment.

Themes: divine beauty, darshan (sacred vision), spiritual ecstasy, soul-bride devotion, love for the Beloved, mystical enchantment
ਸੁੰਦਰ ਸੋਭਾ ਲਾਲ ਗੋਪਾਲ ਦਇਆਲ ਕੀ ਅਪਰ ਅਪਾਰਾ ਰ:
Praising the breathtaking beauty and limitless radiance of the compassionate Sustainer and Beloved Lord. The magnificent splendor and boundless grandeur of the Divine are infinite, beyond measure, and spread throughout existence. Awe-filled adoration celebrating God's boundless grace, nurturing love, and sublime majesty, exalting the boundless nature of the merciful Creator.

Themes: divine beauty, praise and adoration, infinite God, compassion and grace, boundless grandeur, Lord of the Universe, sublime splendor
ਅਪੁਨੇ ਸੇਵਕ ਕੀ ਆਪੇ ਰਾਖੈ ਆਪੇ ਨਾਮੁ ਜਪਾਵੈ ॥:
Affirming total divine agency and protection over the devotee. God Himself preserves the honor, dignity, and safety of His humble servant (sevak), shielding them directly in all circumstances. The Divine also acts as the primary instigator of devotion, prompting and enabling the devotee to engage in simran (loving remembrance) and chant naam (the divine Name). Both preservation and spiritual practice flow entirely from sovereign grace.

Themes: divine protection, preserving honor, naam simran, divine grace, sevak devotee, sovereignty of God
ਭਗਤ ਜਨਾ ਕੀ ਹਰਿ ਜੀਉ ਰਾਖੈ ਜੁਗਿ ਜੁਗਿ ਰਖਦਾ ਆ:
Affirms the eternal nature of divine protection, assuring that God continuously preserves the honor and safety of humble devotees (bhagats). Declares that safeguarding the faithful is an unchanging cosmic law maintained through every age and epoch. Emphasizes absolute trust in divine refuge, offering profound comfort that those surrendered to the Lord are never abandoned or dishonored.

Themes: divine protection, saving devotees, preserving honor, eternal refuge, bhakti devotion, cosmic ages, faith and trust
ਭਗਤ ਤੇਰੇ ਸਭਿ ਪ੍ਰਾਣਪਤਿ ਪ੍ਰੀਤਮ ਤੂੰ ਭਗਤਨ ਕਾ:
Directly praising the Creator as the Master of life's breath and the supreme Beloved of all devotees. The line celebrates the intimate, reciprocal bond of affection and adoration between God and the bhagats (devout seekers), asserting that the Lord sustains their very life and cherishes them, just as the devoted love the Divine above all else.

Themes: bhagat (devotee), divine love, Lord of life, reciprocal affection, devotion, spiritual communion, adoration, beloved God
ਭਗਤਾ ਕੀ ਟੇਕ ਤੂੰ ਸੰਤਾ ਕੀ ਓਟ ਤੂੰ ਸਚਾ ਸਿਰਜਨ:
Addressing the eternal Creator directly in praise and total reliance, declaring God to be the sole anchor, refuge, and protection for devotees and holy beings. The devotee acknowledges absolute dependence on the true Maker, affirming that divine presence and naam (the divine Name) serve as the essential shelter, sanctuary, and sustaining support for all seekers who love the Divine.

Themes: divine refuge, creator as support, devotion, sanctuary, reliance on God, protection for saints, true creator
ਹਰਿ ਜੁਗੁ ਜੁਗੁ ਭਗਤ ਉਪਾਇਆ ਪੈਜ ਰਖਦਾ ਆਇਆ ਰਾਮ:
Declares the eternal custom and sovereign nature of the Divine King, who continuously creates devotees in every cosmic age and unfailingly protects their honor, dignity, and faith during times of trial. Reassures the seeker that the Creator is the timeless guardian and refuge of the devout, perpetually safeguarding those who surrender to divine love.

Themes: divine protection, safeguarding devotee honor, eternal grace across ages, bhagti devotion, sovereign Creator, refuge in God
ਹਮਰੇ ਕਰਮ ਨ ਬਿਚਰਹੁ ਠਾਕੁਰ ਤੁਮ੍ਹ ਪੈਜ ਰਖਹੁ ਅ:
A humble prayer pleading for divine mercy, begging the Master to overlook human faults, past misdeeds, and karmic account. The devotee petitions God to protect the dignity and honor of His servant, relying entirely on unearned grace and unconditional compassion rather than personal merit or righteous actions. It expresses total surrender and vulnerability before divine sovereignty.

Themes: divine mercy, forgiveness of sins, preserving honor, pleading for grace, overcoming karma, humble petition, devotee protection, unconditional love
ਜਾਚਿਕੁ ਮੰਗੈ ਨਿਤ ਨਾਮੁ ਸਾਹਿਬੁ ਕਰੇ ਕਬੂਲੁ ॥:
Declares that when a humble seeker approaches the Divine as a beggar, constantly pleading and praying for naam (the divine Name), the sovereign Master graciously accepts the supplication and fulfills the request. Humility, continual yearning, and earnest devotional begging before the Lord are met with divine grace, acceptance, and spiritual fulfillment rather than worldly desires.

Themes: humble supplication, asking for naam, beggar before God, divine grace, persistent prayer, acceptance of prayer
ਦੇਹਿ ਨਾਮੁ ਸੰਤੋਖੀਆ ਉਤਰੈ ਮਨ ਕੀ ਭੁਖ ॥:
Supplicating the Divine for the gift of naam (the divine Name) to attain true contentment and extinguish worldly cravings. Pleading for spiritual sustenance so the restless hunger, longing, and insatiable desire of the mind are completely satisfied and pacified. Inner peace and fulfillment arise exclusively through receiving divine grace and remembrance.

Themes: naam (divine Name), santokh (contentment), mental hunger, trishna (craving), prayer and supplication, spiritual fulfillment
ਜਾਚਿਕੁ ਨਾਮੁ ਜਾਚੈ ਜਾਚੈ ॥:
Pleading with intense humility and persistent supplication, the seeker assumes the posture of an impoverished beggar constantly begging for naam (the divine Name). This expresses total dependence on God, spiritual poverty, and relentless yearning. The devotee asks for the ultimate alms of divine remembrance and connection, prioritizing spiritual nourishment and grace above worldly desires.

Themes: spiritual begging, humility and supplication, yearning for naam, total dependence on God, persistent prayer, divine alms, seeking grace
ਕਰਹੁ ਕ੍ਰਿਪਾ ਗੋਪਾਲ ਗੋਬਿਦੇ ਅਪਨਾ ਨਾਮੁ ਜਪਾਵਹ:
A direct supplication and humble plea to the Divine Sustainer and Lord of the Universe, begging for divine grace and mercy to enable the chanting and recitation of naam (the divine Name). It confesses human dependence on divine intervention to practice simran (loving remembrance) and meditate, imploring the Creator to bestow the blessing of devotion.

Themes: prayer for grace, simran, chanting naam, divine mercy, supplication, divine sustainer, devotion
ਜਾਚਕੁ ਮੰਗੈ ਦਾਨੁ ਦੇਹਿ ਪਿਆਰਿਆ ॥:
Pleading and praying to the beloved Divine as a humble beggar asking for alms and charity. The seeker adopts a stance of total dependence and humility, imploring God for spiritual nourishment, grace, and the gift of the divine word. It expresses supplication, petitioning the Creator for benevolence, spiritual blessing, and intimate connection with the beloved Master.

Themes: supplication, beggar asking for alms, divine charity, humility, grace, prayer to the beloved, spiritual longing, dependency on God
ਦਰਿ ਮੰਗਤੁ ਜਾਚੈ ਦਾਨੁ ਹਰਿ ਦੀਜੈ ਕ੍ਰਿਪਾ ਕਰਿ:
Pleading for divine grace through radical humility, the seeker stands as a mendicant at God's threshold, begging for spiritual alms and benevolence. The devotee implores the Lord to bestow mercy and grant the supreme gift of divine charity, expressing total dependence and utter surrender before the divine door.

Themes: humility, supplication, begging for grace, divine charity, threshold of God, mercy, total dependence, spiritual alms
ਮਉਲਿਓ ਮਨੁ ਤਨੁ ਹੋਇਓ ਹਰਿਆ ਏਕ ਬੂੰਦ ਜਿਨਿ ਪਾਈ:
Receiving even a single drop of spiritual ambrosia or naam (the divine Name) causes the entire mind and body to blossom and rejuvenate. Describes the profound inner flourishing and revitalization brought by divine grace, comparing spiritual awakening to rain reviving dried vegetation into vibrant, blooming life. Spiritual thirst is quenched and the self is renewed by the smallest measure of sacred essence.

Themes: spiritual rejuvenation, amrit (divine nectar), inner flourishing, divine grace, revitalizing the mind and body, transformation, naam (divine Name)
ਹਰਿ ਰਸੁ ਪੀਵਤ ਸਦ ਹੀ ਰਾਤਾ ॥:
Declares the permanent spiritual intoxication and inner transformation of one who partakes in the sublime divine essence. Imbibing the sweet nectar of naam (the divine Name) leaves the seeker perpetually dyed, soaked, and imbued with divine love. Experiencing the supreme taste of God results in constant, unwavering absorption and eternal spiritual bliss.

Themes: divine nectar, spiritual intoxication, perpetual absorption, love for the Divine, naam, inner fulfillment
ਅੰਮ੍ਰਿਤ ਰਸੁ ਕੀਰਤਨੁ ਹਰਿ ਗਾਈਐ ਅਹਿਨਿਸਿ ਪੂਰਨ:
Exhorts the seeker to sing kirtan (devotional singing of divine praise), declaring it to be the true life-giving ambrosial nectar that bestows spiritual vitality. Engaging in constant praise day and night awakens the complete celestial sound-current within, filling the practitioner with unbroken inner resonance, profound tranquility, and perpetual divine communion.

Themes: kirtan, devotional praise, amrit nectar, unstruck sound current, continuous remembrance, spiritual vitality, inner bliss
ਅੰਮ੍ਰਿਤੁ ਰਸਨਾ ਪੀਉ ਪਿਆਰੀ ॥:
Directly addressing and instructing one's own tongue to drink the spiritual nectar of amrit, tasting the supreme sweetness of naam (the divine Name). Urging the sensory organ of speech and taste to abandon mundane flavors and continuously savor the life-giving divine essence through loving recitation and chanting.

Themes: amrit (ambrosial nectar), taste of naam, instructing the tongue, simran (remembrance), sensory transcendence, devotional chanting
ਤੇਰਾ ਜਨੁ ਰਾਮ ਰਸਾਇਣਿ ਮਾਤਾ ॥:
Declares the ecstatic state of the humble devotee who is utterly intoxicated by the supreme elixir of the Lord's divine Name (naam). The servant of God remains deeply immersed in spiritual bliss, thoroughly absorbed in drinking the sublime alchemical essence of remembrance, and joyful in loving devotion.

Themes: spiritual intoxication, divine nectar, supreme elixir, naam ras, ecstatic devotion, humble servant, absorption in God
ਅੰਮ੍ਰਿਤੁ ਰਸੁ ਪੀਆ ਗੁਰ ਸਬਦੀ ਹਮ ਨਾਮ ਵਿਟਹੁ ਕ:
Drinking the life-giving nectar of spiritual essence through the Guru's shabad (divine teaching), expressing total surrender and reverence to naam (the divine Name). Declaring joyful devotion and sacrifice to the Divine, having experienced the soul-nourishing ambrosial taste of sacred wisdom revealed through the Guru's word.

Themes: amrit ras, Guru shabad, surrender and sacrifice, devotion to naam, spiritual nectar, divine experience, inner nourishment
ਰਸੁ ਅੰਮ੍ਰਿਤੁ ਨਾਮੁ ਰਸੁ ਅਤਿ ਭਲਾ ਕਿਤੁ ਬਿਧਿ:
Praises naam (the divine Name) as the supreme, life-giving ambrosial nectar and asks with earnest yearning how one can obtain and taste this sublime essence. The seeker expresses spiritual thirst, inquiring by what method or path one can partake of this ultimate sweetness and consume the life-transforming elixir of the Divine.

Themes: amrit (ambrosial nectar), naam (divine Name), spiritual longing, seeking guidance, divine taste, spiritual hunger
ਬਿਖੈ ਬਨੁ ਫੀਕਾ ਤਿਆਗਿ ਰੀ ਸਖੀਏ ਨਾਮੁ ਮਹਾ ਰਸੁ:
Exhorts the seeker or soul-bride companion to abandon the insipid, toxic water of sensory vices, corruption, and worldly poisons, urging them instead to drink the sublime, supreme nectar of naam (the divine Name). It contrasts the empty, tasteless gratification of sinful material desires with the profound spiritual sweetness of divine remembrance, commanding an intentional turning away from corrupt pleasures toward sacred sustenance.

Themes: renouncing corruption, sensory vices, divine nectar, naam amrit, spiritual thirst, soul bride companion, worldly detachment
ਕਬੀਰ ਬਿਰਹੁ ਭੁਯੰਗਮੁ ਮਨਿ ਬਸੈ ਮੰਤੁ ਨ ਮਾਨੈ ਕ:
Portraying the consuming agony of spiritual separation as a venomous serpent dwelling inside the mind, immune to any magical spell or mantra. Declaring that once the profound pain of longing for the Divine takes hold, no worldly remedy, charm, or intellectual effort can cure or alleviate that inner yearning. Spiritual alienation and love-sickness entirely overtake consciousness.

Themes: spiritual longing, pain of separation, birha, serpent metaphor, inner agony, yearning for union, divine love
ਹਰਿ ਬਿਨੁ ਕਿਉ ਜੀਵਾ ਮੇਰੀ ਮਾਈ ॥:
A seeker cries out in profound spiritual yearning and agony of separation, addressing their mother to confess the impossibility of sustaining life without the Divine. Expresses absolute emotional and spiritual dependence on God and naam (the divine Name), declaring that existence becomes unbearable and restless without divine communion. The soul articulates deep love and helplessness in the ache of detachment.

Themes: yearning for the Divine, pain of separation, spiritual longing, dependence on God, love for the Lord, birha
ਪ੍ਰਭ ਮਿਲਬੇ ਕਉ ਪ੍ਰੀਤਿ ਮਨਿ ਲਾਗੀ ॥:
Declares an awakening of deep spiritual love and yearning within the mind to unite with God. Expresses the soul's intense longing, affectionate thirst, and devotion to meet the Divine Beloved, marking the inner arising of genuine attachment to the Creator and a heartfelt desire for divine communion.

Themes: longing for God, divine love, union with the Beloved, spiritual thirst, yearning, devotion, awakening of love
ਹਰਿ ਦਰਸਨ ਕਉ ਮੇਰਾ ਮਨੁ ਬਹੁ ਤਪਤੈ ਜਿਉ ਤ੍ਰਿਖਾ:
Confessing an intense, agonizing spiritual longing for darshan (the divine vision of the Lord). The mind burns and writhes in separation, comparing its acute spiritual craving to a parched person dying of thirst without water. It articulates the acute pain of separation (birha), desperate love, and the vital necessity of divine realization for spiritual survival.

Themes: darshan, spiritual longing, thirst for God, pangs of separation, intense love, craving divine presence, agony of mind
ਬਾਝਹੁ ਪਿਆਰੇ ਕੋਇ ਨ ਸਾਰੇ ਏਕਲੜੀ ਕੁਰਲਾਏ ॥:
Lamenting the soul-bride's utter isolation and sorrow without the Divine Beloved. Apart from God, no worldly entity cares for or inquires after the soul, leaving her to weep and wail in anguish alone in the wilderness of worldly existence. Expresses deep vulnerability, abandonment, and painful yearning in separation, recognizing that only the Divine offers true shelter, compassion, and enduring companionship.

Themes: separation from God, soul-bride, loneliness and isolation, longing for the beloved, viraha, helplessness, divine refuge, worldly alienation
ਮਨਿ ਬੈਰਾਗੁ ਭਇਆ ਦਰਸਨੁ ਦੇਖਣੈ ਕਾ ਚਾਉ ॥:
Expressing an intense devotional state where the mind turns detached from worldly pursuits and becomes consumed by deep spiritual longing. Dispassion from maya (worldly attachment) transforms into an ardent desire and joyful craving for the blessed vision (darshan) of the Divine. Confesses an inner awakening of love, yearning for direct communion with God, and abandonment of transient material concerns.

Themes: bairag (spiritual detachment), darshan (divine vision), longing for God, devotional yearning, divine love, thirst for union, detachment from maya
ਘਰਿ ਆਵਹੁ ਚਿਰੀ ਵਿਛੁੰਨਿਆ ਮਿਲੁ ਸਬਦਿ ਗੁਰੂ ਪ੍:
A longing soul-bride pleads with the Divine Lord to return to the home of her heart and end an agonizing, prolonged separation. Yearning for intimate union and spiritual reunion, she begs her divine Husband to meet and dwell within her consciousness through the transformative wisdom of the Guru’s shabad (divine word).

Themes: birha and separation, yearning for God, soul-bride, inner dwelling, guru shabad, divine union, longing for the spouse Lord
ਪਿਰ ਦੋਸੁ ਨਾਹੀ ਸੁਖਹ ਦਾਤੇ ਹਉ ਵਿਛੁੜੀ ਬੁਰਿਆਰ:
The soul-bride acknowledges personal responsibility for her separation from God, absolving the Divine Spouse and bestower of all peace of any blame. She confesses her own shortcomings, vices, and misdeeds as the true cause of spiritual estrangement. This is an admission of guilt, a lament of disconnection, and an acceptance that human error and ego alienate the self from the flawless Creator.

Themes: personal accountability, separation from God, soul-bride, confession of faults, divine perfection, spiritual estrangement, giver of peace
ਆਉ ਜੀ ਤੂ ਆਉ ਹਮਾਰੈ ਹਰਿ ਜਸੁ ਸ੍ਰਵਨ ਸੁਨਾਵਨਾ:
An earnest plea and loving invitation welcoming the Guru and the Divine into the home of one's heart. The seeker begs the beloved Lord to enter their inner sanctuary and recite the Lord's praises directly into their ears. It expresses deep longing for holy association, yearning to listen to sacred discourse, and seeking spiritual awakening through receptive listening and devotional communion.

Themes: longing for the divine, inner sanctuary, hearing divine praises, invitation to the Guru, listening to kirtan, yearning for union, devotional prayer
ਆਉ ਹਮਾਰੈ ਰਾਮ ਪਿਆਰੇ ਜੀਉ ॥:
Directly pleading with and welcoming the beloved Lord to enter and dwell within one's heart. It expresses an intimate longing for divine presence, inviting God as a cherished companion into the devotee's inner self. The soul calls out in tender love, seeking union, communion, and the immediate indwelling of the divine Beloved.

Themes: yearning for God, divine union, longing, indwelling presence, divine love, intimacy with God, supplication
ਬਿਨਵੰਤਿ ਨਾਨਕ ਦਇਆ ਧਾਰਹੁ ਘਰਿ ਆਵਹੁ ਨਾਹ ਪਿਆਰ:
Pleading for divine grace and mercy, the soul-bride earnestly begs her beloved Divine Husband to return and dwell within the home of her heart. A devotional supplication longing for spiritual union, seeking the intimate presence of God to manifest within the inner consciousness and end the pain of separation.

Themes: yearning for God, soul-bride, divine grace, inner dwelling, spiritual union, devotional prayer, intimacy with the Divine
ਮੋਹਨ ਘਰਿ ਆਵਹੁ ਕਰਉ ਜੋਦਰੀਆ ॥:
Pleading with the enchanting Divine to enter and abide within the inner home of the heart. The soul-bride makes a humble supplication, yearning for intimate communion and direct spiritual realization. This entreaty expresses devotional longing, surrender, and deep affection, begging the captivating Lord to dwell consciously within one's consciousness and manifest His presence.

Themes: longing for union, soul-bride, humble supplication, divine indwelling, devotion, inner home, love for God
ਹਮ ਘਰਿ ਸਾਜਨ ਆਏ ॥:
Declaring joyful arrival and spiritual fulfillment as the Divine Friend manifests within the home of the heart. The seeker celebrates inner union, welcoming the beloved Lord into personal consciousness. The arrival of the sacred companion transforms the inner self from separation into blissful communion, marking the manifestation of God inside one's own being.

Themes: divine union, inner presence, beloved friend, heart as home, spiritual joy, realization of God, sacred communion
ਪਹਿਲੈ ਪਹਰੈ ਫੁਲੜਾ ਫਲੁ ਭੀ ਪਛਾ ਰਾਤਿ ॥:
Contrasts the spiritual value of different times of night, declaring that devotion during the early evening blossoms like a delicate flower, while worship in the late night and predawn ambrosial hours (amrit vela) yields full, nourishing fruit. Uses botanical imagery of blossoming and fruiting to urge rising early for simran (loving remembrance) and divine contemplation, establishing predawn meditation as the peak of spiritual attainment.

Themes: amrit vela, predawn devotion, spiritual fruit, meditation timing, simran, discipline of prayer, spiritual reward
ਕਬੀਰ ਸੂਤਾ ਕਿਆ ਕਰਹਿ ਉਠਿ ਕਿ ਨ ਜਪਹਿ ਮੁਰਾਰਿ:
Admonishes the mind and awakens the mortal from the slumber of maya (worldly illusion and attachment). Demands an end to spiritual lethargy and wasted life, urging the seeker to rise up and engage in simran (loving remembrance) of the Divine Lord. It contrasts negligent, unconscious living with purposeful, vigilant devotion and meditation on God.

Themes: spiritual awakening, overcoming maya, simran, urgency of devotion, admonishing the mind, remembrance of God, purpose of life
ਪਰਭਾਤੇ ਪ੍ਰਭ ਨਾਮੁ ਜਪਿ ਗੁਰ ਕੇ ਚਰਣ ਧਿਆਇ ॥:
Instructs the seeker to rise at the ambrosial dawn to practice simran (loving remembrance) of the divine Name and meditate upon the Guru's feet, symbolizing deep humility, reverence, and surrender. Early morning spiritual discipline combines chanting God's Name with enshrinement of the spiritual guide's wisdom in the heart, establishing devotional contemplation as the foundation of daily life.

Themes: early morning prayer, amrit vela, chanting naam, guru devotion, surrender at guru's feet, spiritual discipline, remembrance
ਝਾਲਾਘੇ ਉਠਿ ਨਾਮੁ ਜਪਿ ਨਿਸਿ ਬਾਸੁਰ ਆਰਾਧਿ ॥:
Direct instruction commanding the seeker to rise at the ambrosial early dawn and recite naam (the divine Name), extending this contemplation into continuous remembrance day and night. It prescribes a strict spiritual discipline of early morning meditation followed by constant, ceaseless devotion at every hour, transforming daily existence into unceasing worship of the Divine.

Themes: early morning prayer, amrit vela, simran, continuous devotion, spiritual discipline, naam meditation, daily remembrance
ਬਾਬੀਹਾ ਅੰਮ੍ਰਿਤ ਵੇਲੈ ਬੋਲਿਆ ਤਾਂ ਦਰਿ ਸੁਣੀ ਪ:
Declaring that supplications made during the pre-dawn hours are heard and accepted in the divine presence. Using the image of the thirsty rainbird calling out at amrit vela (the ambrosial pre-dawn hours), the seeker's early morning longing, devotion, and sincere petition are affirmed as reaching the Lord's court to receive grace and spiritual nourishment.

Themes: amrit vela, early morning prayer, rainbird metaphor, answered prayer, spiritual longing, divine grace, petition and ardaas
ਛਾਤੀ ਸੀਤਲ ਮਨੁ ਸੁਖੀ ਛੰਤ ਗੋਬਿਦ ਗੁਨ ਗਾਇ ॥:
Singing praises and hymns of the Lord of the Universe cools the burning chest and brings total tranquility to the mind. The inner fire of worldly desires and agitation is extinguished, replaced by profound emotional soothing, inner peace, and spiritual comfort. Uttering divine qualities pacifies restless thoughts, cooling the heart and satisfying the soul.

Themes: singing praises, kirtan, cooling the heart, mental peace, inner tranquility, extinguishing desire, spiritual comfort
ਜੋਗੁ ਬਨਿਆ ਤੇਰਾ ਕੀਰਤਨੁ ਗਾਈ ॥੧॥:
Singing kirtan (devotional praises of the Divine) is declared to be the true yoga or spiritual union. Musical worship and glorification of the Lord fulfill all mystical practices, granting both spiritual liberation and supreme inner contentment. The soul attains complete communion and yogic realization simply by chanting and celebrating the virtues of the Creator rather than through austere asceticism.

Themes: kirtan, spiritual union, yoga, singing divine praise, mystical communion, devotion over asceticism, spiritual realization
ਹਉ ਅਨਦਿਨੁ ਹਰਿ ਨਾਮੁ ਕੀਰਤਨੁ ਕਰਉ ॥:
Declaring dedicated personal devotion through constant praise of the Divine. The seeker commits to singing kirtan (devotional singing of praises) and reciting the divine Name day and night without interruption. It expresses a state of unceasing, round-the-clock remembrance (simran) and ongoing glorification of God as one's central spiritual practice.

Themes: kirtan, divine praise, continuous remembrance, naam simran, perpetual devotion, chanting God's name, spiritual practice
ਰੁਣ ਝੁਣੋ ਸਬਦੁ ਅਨਾਹਦੁ ਨਿਤ ਉਠਿ ਗਾਈਐ ਸੰਤਨ ਕ:
Instructing the devotee to practice daily discipline by rising early to sing praises of the Divine in the company of the holy (sadh sangat). Chanting sacred melody joins one with the unstruck sound current (anahad shabad, the continuous inner celestial resonance). It urges continuous participation in collective worship, making devotion an active, daily routine centered on melodious praise and sacred association.

Themes: amrit vela, daily discipline, sadh sangat, anahad shabad, kirtan, unstruck melody, devotional singing, divine praise
ਸਾਧੋ ਗੋਬਿੰਦ ਕੇ ਗੁਨ ਗਾਵਉ ॥:
Exhorting and instructing spiritual seekers and holy companions to continuously sing the glorious praises and virtues of the Lord of the universe. It calls the devout to engage in devotional worship, chanting divine attributes and cultivating constant remembrance through sacred song. The directive establishes praising the creator's excellence as the essential spiritual practice and primary duty of the holy assembly.

Themes: singing divine praises, kirtan, sadhu, devotional adoration, chanting God's virtues, holy company, spiritual exhortation, remembering the Lord
ਨਿਰਬਾਣ ਕੀਰਤਨੁ ਗਾਵਹੁ ਕਰਤੇ ਕਾ ਨਿਮਖ ਸਿਮਰਤ ਜ:
Instructs the seeker to sing kirtan (devotional singing of divine praises) of the Creator while free from worldly desires and material attachments. Engaging in simran (loving remembrance) of the Divine, even for a single fleeting moment, grants complete spiritual liberation and delivers the soul from vices, illusion, and existential bondage.

Themes: kirtan, praising the Creator, detachment from desire, simran, instant liberation, freedom from vice, devotional singing
ਮਨ ਮੀਠ ਤੁਹਾਰੋ ਕੀਓ ॥੧॥ ਰਹਾਉ ॥:
Declaring total surrender and joyful acceptance of the divine will (hukam), the mind finds whatever the Divine ordains or does to be profoundly sweet and pleasing. It conveys complete contentment without complaint, resentment, or blame toward anyone, resting in equanimity by viewing every occurrence as a benevolent act of God.

Themes: accepting divine will, hukam, sweet will, contentment, absence of complaint, surrender, equanimity, devotion
ਮੀਤ ਕੇ ਕਰਤਬ ਕੁਸਲ ਸਮਾਨਾ ॥੧॥:
Declaring total acceptance and sweet surrender to divine will, experiencing every deed and working of God as pure joy, bliss, and comfort. The devotee relates to the Lord as an intimate Beloved Friend, finding complete peace, welfare, and contentment in whatever the Divine does. Accepting the divine ordinance without resistance, seeing absolute goodness and serenity in all divine actions.

Themes: divine will, sweet acceptance of hukam, God as intimate friend, inner peace, spiritual contentment, joy in divine ordinance, surrender
ਸਰਬ ਸੁਖ ਆਨੰਦ ਮੰਗਲ ਰਸ ਮਾਨਿ ਗੋਬਿੰਦੈ ਆਗਿਓ ॥:
Declaring that ultimate peace, supreme joy, bliss, and all spiritual delights are attained through accepting and obeying the divine will and command of the Sovereign Lord. Surrendering to the divine decree brings complete contentment, eradicating all distress. Submitting to God's order transforms existence into an ongoing celebration of profound happiness, spiritual relish, and satisfaction.

Themes: divine will, obedience to God, surrender, spiritual joy, inner peace, contentment, accepting divine decree
ਖਿਨ ਮਹਿ ਥਾਪਿ ਉਥਾਪਨਹਾਰਾ ਆਪਨ ਹਾਥਿ ਮਤਾਤ ॥੧॥:
Declaring the supreme omnipotence and absolute sovereignty of the Divine, who creates and destroys, establishes and dismantles the entire universe in a single instant. Ultimate authority and all cosmic decisions rest solely in His control, demonstrating that every outcome, judgment, and power belongs to the Creator alone rather than any mortal agency.

Themes: divine omnipotence, supreme sovereignty, creation and destruction, instantaneous power, divine will, absolute authority, cosmic control
ਨਾਨਕ ਨਾਮੁ ਧਿਆਈਐ ਕਾਰਜੁ ਆਵੈ ਰਾਸਿ ॥੧॥:
Instructs the devotee to remember and meditate on naam (the divine Name), assuring that contemplation brings all tasks, endeavors, and spiritual affairs to successful completion. Engraining divine remembrance in the mind ensures the fruition of every undertaking, resolving difficulties and bringing total fulfillment to both worldly work and spiritual purpose.

Themes: naam simran, divine assistance, resolution of affairs, successful completion, spiritual fulfillment, meditation
ਕਾਰਜੁ ਤੇਰਾ ਹੋਵੈ ਪੂਰਾ ਹਰਿ ਹਰਿ ਹਰਿ ਗੁਣ ਗਾਇ:
Admonishing and instructing one's own mind to continually sing the virtues and praises of the Divine. Chanting and engaging in simran (loving remembrance) ensures that all tasks, worldly affairs, and spiritual endeavors reach complete fulfillment and successful resolution. Devotional praise guarantees the accomplishment of life's purpose and the perfection of one's deeds.

Themes: singing divine praises, resolving affairs, spiritual success, self-admonition to mind, simran, fulfilling purpose, divine grace
ਨਾਨਕ ਨਾਮੁ ਅਰਾਧਣਾ ਕਾਰਜੁ ਆਵੈ ਰਾਸਿ ॥੮॥:
Instructing the mind to contemplate naam (the divine Name) with total assurance that all endeavors are perfectly fulfilled and resolved through remembrance. Meditating on the Lord accomplishes the ultimate purpose of human life, bringing spiritual completion, settling all worldly and spiritual tasks, and yielding total fruition.

Themes: naam simran, fulfillment of life purpose, resolution of affairs, spiritual success, divine contemplation, accomplishment of tasks
ਸਭੇ ਕਾਜ ਸਵਾਰਿਐ ਜਾ ਤੁਧੁ ਭਾਵੰਦਾ ॥੭॥:
Declares that all undertakings, tasks, and affairs of life are perfected and brought to successful completion solely through divine will and pleasure. Attaining the favor and grace of the Divine resolves every difficulty and fulfills all endeavors. Success in both worldly and spiritual pursuits rests entirely on being pleasing to God, emphasizing surrender to divine approval rather than relying on self-effort.

Themes: divine grace, divine will (hukam), fulfillment of affairs, pleasing God, total surrender, spiritual success, reliance on God
ਸਗਲ ਮਨੋਰਥ ਪੂਰਨ ਹੋਏ ਕਦੇ ਨ ਹੋਇ ਦੁਖਾਲਾ ਜੀਉ:
Declares the total fulfillment of every heartfelt desire, need, and spiritual aspiration, resulting in eternal freedom from grief, pain, and sorrow. Attaining divine contentment removes all distress, affliction, and lack, leaving the soul in perpetual satisfaction and peace, permanently protected from future misery and anguish.

Themes: spiritual fulfillment, freedom from suffering, divine contentment, elimination of sorrow, satisfaction of desires, eternal peace, bliss
